P1.evidence: No setter is named anywhere on the call and no application or setter notes were read back, so P1a could not apply. The frame ran but three-part rather than four: 'in order to get there, I need to get to know you a little bit better. Where are you trying to get to? What have you tried? And yeah, just tell me more about how we can actually help you' — where you are now was never framed. No 'does that work?' agreement was sought. The open question landed cleanly and produced a long unprompted answer.

P2.evidence: Weight and height captured — 'So how much do you weigh right now?' / '198. And I'm 5'8"' — but age was never asked and is absent from the record entirely. Work covered properly, including whether he can stand: 'Are you able, like, during your work, can you stand up?' Health conditions, own or hereditary, never asked; only injuries were. Injuries probed thoroughly, including onset and duration: 'Was it always difficult, or it deteriorated over the years?' and 'when was that?' Training week and current results both asked directly: 'how many times per week do you work out actually right now?' and 'what results did you get?' Diet covered in detail including the comfort-food question. Sleep never asked, energy never asked — the prospect volunteered 'having that extra energy to say yes when they wanted to do something' as part of his why.

P3.evidence: Goals opened with 'what's the main target here? Like, what's your main goal?' rather than the scripted one-thing-you-would-change, and the mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered. The can't-do question ran twice and well: 'apart from paddle that you cannot do, are there anything else that you cannot perform because of the back or something like that?' and 'Are you missing anything else, like any other sports that you like to play?' The bridge to the deeper driver was the strongest move on the call and the rep even risked the sale on it: 'if there is no like deeper purpose in this, I don't know if this is actually a thing for you... do you really need it, yeah?' That produced the daughters. Who-else-does-it-impact was never asked — the daughters came unprompted. The rep then drove the legacy frame hard: 'That's the strongest why that a man can get... the ones that their why is their kids... you have this vision if you don't do it... you won't be able to play with them.' The reflect-back was implicit ('Now we're talking') rather than the scripted 'so this isn't really about X'.

P4.evidence: Past attempts surfaced fully — CrossFit L1 background, current Pat Damiano programme, Trevor's YouTube workouts — with 'Okay, you're doing that program right now?' and 'how long have you been doing that?' Outcome asked directly: 'what results did you get?' The self-reliance challenge ran early and hard, which is the P4f move: 'since you've been already a CrossFit athlete and trainer, why us? Why Trevor? Why not do it by yourself?' The prospect named his own gap without being fed it: 'I just tend to gravitate towards certain movements and start developing weaknesses or blind spots, and I'd just rather just pick something up.' P4c is only partial because the current approach is working, so 'why didn't it stick' had no purchase and the rep did not adapt it.

P5.evidence: A compressed consequence gesture rather than the phase: 'you have this vision if you don't do it. Right... A few years down. And you won't be able to play with them, and you still want to do it, right?' It was delivered as an agreement the prospect nodded along to, not as a question forcing him to articulate the cost himself. No two-year question, no willing-to-settle, no why-not, no line in the sand. The consequence was left thin, which mattered later — against a $45/month alternative that is visibly working, the cost of not changing was never made concrete.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran inverted and the answer went unchallenged: 'Do you feel what you're doing right now will get you there, in terms of the health and longevity?' — 'I think it will. I think it will.' The rep asked whether the prospect's existing free approach would work, got a yes, and never dismantled it; that yes is the seed of the objection that killed the call. The all-in and isolate questions did run — 'do you want to actually, do you want to do this?... if you want to do this, and there's no, any other constraints apart from the financial... are you going to be committed to actually showing up?' — but after the price, not before it. No clear pre-presentation yes was obtained; the rep moved into the offer on 'Good.' and 'no questions yet.'

P11.evidence: Payment collection was attempted — a third-party financing link was sent in Zoom chat and opened live — but nothing was collected: 'So I don't think it's gonna, I don't think I'm going to be able to do it.' Steps 2 to 4 were unreachable with no sale: no Trevor onboarding call, no agreement email, no Skool or questionnaire instructions. The rep closed out cleanly and without pressure: 'Fair play... the door is open.'

objection_plays.detail: No think-about-it. The prospect gave a definite no on the call rather than deferring.
No spouse gate — he is mid-divorce and the decision is entirely his.

Isolation ran: 'if you want to do this, and there's no, any other constraints apart from the financial... obstacle that we can talk about.' The break-it-up move ran: 'if we could split it in some way that would be more digestible is that something that you could look into it'. But the financial picture was almost entirely skipped — the rep asked one question, 'Is it that you don't have the whole amount or what is it actually?', and then jumped straight to third-party credit. Cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available versus used credit, and investments were all never asked. The HOW-not-SHOULD-I frame was never spoken; the nearest thing was 'if there's a will there's a way.' Skipping the financial picture is why the rep could not tell the difference between a prospect who could not pay and one who would not, and ended up sending a credit application to a man mid-divorce-asset-split.

Trigger clear: 'it doesn't feel like it's the time right now to spend 4k on that' and 'finding that stability before committing.' One OD move ran, inside a badly merged transcript block — 'when's gonna be the perfect time, there's no such thing' and 'there's always something'. The prospect immediately reframed past it: 'I don't know if it's about the perfect time but it's about not being... reckless but it's measured I guess.' The rep did not follow with the metabolism-and-injuries-compound move, the only-thing-you-can-control-is-right-now move, or the show-up-and-everything-else-is-handled move, and let the prospect's reframe stand.
No fear or doubt about the method. He is an ex-CrossFit coach already using Trevor's free content and confident in the modality.

Script gap, second recorded instance and the cleanest one yet. The prospect is on a $45/month membership that has produced 40 lb of loss in three months and stated the comparison himself: '$45 per month in a membership... Versus, what is it? 1,333 per month... it's a pretty big leap.' Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay; here the blocker was value ratio against a functioning substitute. The rep had nothing to run — no ROI framing, no what-the-membership-cannot-do, no reference to the shoulder instability and back history that a one-to-one could programme around and a generic membership cannot. He went to the emotional why instead, which the prospect had already agreed with and which did not move the number.

notes: Genuinely good discovery — the why-not-do-it-yourself challenge and the willingness to talk the prospect out of buying are both better than the script asks for — then three compounding errors at the back end. First, he asked whether the prospect's current free programme would get him there, was told yes, and left it standing. Second, he invented a three-month $4,000 tier before any resistance appeared, which both broke the price book and reduced the value he then had to defend. Third, facing a working $45/month alternative he had no play and reached for consumer credit instead of the financial picture. Coach: never ask a self-sufficient prospect if his current approach is working unless you intend to dismantle the answer, and run the full OC financial picture before sending anyone a credit link.
